annotations.title: Find and redact API keys, tokens, private keys and passwords in text

description: Use when the user asks whether some text contains secrets, or before you paste, commit, share, log or send code, a .env file, a diff, config, logs, a stack trace or a prompt that might contain credentials, for example "did I leak a key in this?", "is this safe to post?" or "redact the secrets in this log". Detects 48 services by exact key format (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini/Google, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, Stripe, Supabase, AWS, GitHub, GitLab, npm, PyPI, Slack, Discord, Twilio, SendGrid, Resend, Shopify, Cloudflare and more) plus PEM private keys, database URLs with passwords, JWTs, Authorization headers and high-entropy values in variables named like secret, token, api_key or password. It verifies what it can deterministically: GitHub token CRC32 checksums, JWT and Supabase key role and expiry (service_role vs anon), documented example keys and placeholders, and NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables that ship to every browser. Returns findings with severity (critical, high, medium, public, info), line and column, a masked preview (never the full secret), why it matters, the fix and the provider's revoke URL, plus a redacted copy with labels like [STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_1]. Text is processed in memory to answer and is not stored. Limits: format-based, so a random secret with a neutral name can be missed; it never tests keys against providers; up to 200,000 characters. For secrets the user should not send anywhere, point them to https://spill.clawhard.com, which runs entirely in the browser.

redact_public_keys.description: false (default): keep keys that are meant to be public (Stripe pk_, Supabase anon or publishable, Mapbox pk.) in the redacted copy so the code still runs. true: hide them too.

text.description: The text to scan: code, a diff, .env, config, logs, a stack trace, a chat or a prompt.
